metadata.description: Self-hosted best-practice plugins: UI/UX stacks, frameworks, databases, architecture, design patterns, testing, security, API design, dev environments, and the taskmaster clarification-to-execution workflow suite.

plugins.name: ui-ux
plugins.description: UI/UX best practices with per-stack skills: shadcn/ui, ReUI, Aceternity UI, Astryx, Tailwind — plus a design-tokens skill (spacing/type/radius/elevation/motion scales + semantic color tiering), a theming-system skill, theme creation with a live colour preview, a /ui-ux:build entry point, and ui-ux-reviewer + ui-ux-engineer agents.

plugins.name: craft-layer
plugins.description: Create unique, animated, informative web apps (CRM, SaaS, landing pages) across React, Tailwind, Vue, Next, Nuxt, and Laravel. /craft-layer:craft runs the studio pipeline end to end — creative direction, design research, asset sourcing with a licence gate, theming and component build via ui-ux, and a tiered motion system (Framer, anime.js, Three.js/R3F, Lottie/Rive, sprites) with reduced-motion and reduced-bundle fallbacks. /craft-layer:sections guides per-section decisions, /craft-layer:audit reviews a shipped tree, and ultra-craft escalates a run with live web research and a red-team of the result. Requires ui-ux and a11y; reuses threejs.

plugins.name: registry-source
plugins.description: Read component registries from the source, never from memory. Ships two MCP servers: a dependency-free local one with live list/search/get across Aceternity, shadcn and Magic UI — 24h-cached, every answer carrying its source URL, fetch date and a stale flag — plus ReUI's own hosted server, so installing the plugin delivers it. Flags components pulling a 3D/particle runtime so bundle cost is known before install. Never holds a licence key; ReUI auth is a browser sign-in the user completes.

plugins.name: react
plugins.description: React data-layer discipline across two skills: server state (TanStack Query/SWR/RTK Query — cache keys and invalidation, mutations and optimistic updates, paginated/infinite data, keeping server data out of useState) and data grids (TanStack Table v9/v8 API detection, column defs, controlled table state, server-side pagination, TanStack Virtual, shadcn DataTable composition).

plugins.name: react-native
plugins.description: React Native best practices: list performance, navigation, platform-specific code, animations.

plugins.name: vue3
plugins.description: Vue 3 best practices: script setup, composables, ref/reactive pitfalls, Pinia.

plugins.name: nextjs
plugins.description: Next.js best practices: App Router server/client boundaries, opt-in caching (fetch, revalidate, use cache), server actions as public endpoints, route handlers, streaming with Suspense, metadata API, next/image and next/font — version-aware from 14 through 16.

plugins.name: nuxt
plugins.description: Nuxt best practices: Nitro server routes, hybrid rendering route rules, useFetch/useAsyncData payload dedup, useState SSR-safe state, auto-imports discipline, runtimeConfig env overrides, SEO meta.

plugins.name: php
plugins.description: PHP best practices: strict types, === discipline, PSR conventions, version-aware 8.1-8.5 leverage map pinned to the composer.json floor, exceptions, DateTimeImmutable, boundary security, static analysis.

plugins.name: laravel
plugins.description: Laravel best practices: Eloquent N+1 prevention, form requests, service layer, queues, policies, a per-version leverage map (Laravel 11/12/13), and mass-assignment security — plus the shared backend-engineer worker (PHP/Laravel) the php/laravel review commands route their fixes to.

plugins.name: livewire
plugins.description: Livewire 3/4 best practices: component conventions, wire:model modifiers, performance, Alpine interop.

plugins.name: sql
plugins.description: Engine-agnostic SQL best practices: sargable predicates, join correctness, indexing logic, NULL three-valued logic, transactions, constraints, keyset pagination, safe migrations, parameterization.

plugins.name: mysql
plugins.description: MySQL 8.0+ best practices: InnoDB clustered-PK design, utf8mb4, strict sql_mode, online DDL, gap locks, version leverage 8.0 through 8.4 and 9.7 LTS, EXPLAIN ANALYZE.

plugins.name: mariadb
plugins.description: MariaDB 10.6+ best practices: not-MySQL divergences, RETURNING, sequences, system-versioned tables, UUID type, uca1400 collations, JSON-as-text reality, Galera awareness.

plugins.name: postgresql
plugins.description: PostgreSQL 14+ best practices: MVCC and vacuum reality, rich types (timestamptz, jsonb, uuid), index arsenal (partial, expression, GIN, BRIN, CONCURRENTLY), lock-aware migrations, ON CONFLICT/RETURNING, version leverage through 17/18.

plugins.name: code-architecture
plugins.description: Engineering process: plan-before-code, YAGNI, SOLID principles applied with judgment, task orchestration, work verification — enforced by a blocking Stop hook that refuses a completion claim when files were edited but nothing ran afterward — low-cognitive-load code, KISS/DRY simplicity principles. Owns code-level structure — units, interfaces, file placement; defers system-level topology (service boundaries, scaling, caching) to the system-design plugin.

plugins.name: api-docs-first
plugins.description: Docs before claims, both directions: verify current official API/SDK docs before writing integration code (UserPromptSubmit reminder + /api-docs-first:check), and keep your own docs true after a change with the merged docs-upkeep drift scan — README claims, changelog gaps, stale examples, dead links (/api-docs-first:drift).

plugins.name: taskmaster
plugins.description: Idea-to-execution clarification: brainstorm fuzzy ideas into approved designs, grill requirements until zero ambiguity, deliberate the implementation approach with a blind four-persona round (via the approaches plugin when installed; inline 2-3 approaches otherwise), decide visual choices with mockups, validate whole experiences with an interactive clickable demo, then emit milestone-grouped single-prompt task cards. Outputs live under taskmaster-docs/ (no collision with a project's own docs/).

plugins.name: design-preview
plugins.description: Real-component visual decisions for Vite (React or Vue/Nuxt) and Laravel Blade/Livewire projects: renders 2-3 candidate variants with the project's OWN components on its own dev server via a scratch HTML entry (zero edits to existing files), behind a strict consent gate with guaranteed cleanup. Escalation tier above static shell mockups — falls back to them when Vite is absent. Includes /design-preview:preview.

plugins.name: shadcn-studio
plugins.description: Greenfield interactive shadcn staging: stands up a self-contained shadcn + Vite (Tailwind v4) sandbox on its own dev server and renders agent-authored component variants side by side — real interactivity (sort/filter/dialog), not static HTML. For idea-stage / non-React work where design-preview cannot run (no host Vite+React app). Consent-gated, scratch outside the work tree, verified cleanup, static-shell fallback. Includes /shadcn-studio:stage.

plugins.name: git-workflow
plugins.description: Git workflow discipline: isolated worktrees for feature work, a structured finish protocol for development branches (verify, present options, merge/PR/park, clean up), and review-exchange rigor — what to include when requesting review, and technical verification before implementing received feedback. Includes /git-workflow:finish.

plugins.name: debugging
plugins.description: Systematic debugging: root cause before any fix — reproduce first, read the actual error, isolate with hypothesis tests and bisection, one change at a time, verify against the original symptom; escalation rule after three failed fixes. Ships a delegatable debugger agent for handing off the long reproduce-bisect investigation. Includes /debugging:debug.

plugins.name: task-runner
plugins.description: Disciplined task execution: one task at a time, scope locked to the task, bounded verify-fix inner loop per task, no drift, no unbounded outer loop. Completion means every check passed with evidence. Ships the shared task-executor agent — the delegatable 'apply the fixes' sink every review routes to — and a PostToolUse scope-lock tripwire that flags edits outside the current task's declared files. Includes parallel-planning: computed subagents-vs-inline verdict with dependency levels, agent count, and speedup estimate via /task-runner:plan.

plugins.name: stack-scan
plugins.description: Inventory the project's actual stack: manifests and lockfiles (composer, npm/yarn/pnpm/bun), runtimes, engine constraints, docker images. Reports required vs installed versions and flags drift, missing locks, and EOL majors.

plugins.name: plugin-scout
plugins.description: Scan the current project's manifests and suggest which cc-plugins-marketplace plugins to install — stack-matched tier and always-useful tier — then install the picked ones after confirmation. Includes /plugin-scout:suggest.

plugins.name: vercel-skills-scout
plugins.description: Scout skills.sh — Vercel's open agent-skills directory — for third-party skills matching the project's stack: scans manifests, queries the skills.sh search API, reports each hit with provenance (source repo, install count, skills.sh URL), previews the picked skills' SKILL.md before anything lands, then installs only explicit picks via npx skills add — project-level, never global, never auto-installed. Includes /vercel-skills-scout:suggest.

plugins.name: testing
plugins.description: Testing best practices: test pyramid and what to actually test, Pest/PHPUnit and Vitest/Jest idioms, Playwright/Dusk e2e discipline, factories and fixtures, mocking boundaries, flaky-test causes, coverage traps — plus the TDD workflow (red-green-refactor, red-green regression proof for bug fixes). Includes /testing:review, /testing:flake-hunt and a test-engineer worker agent.

plugins.name: security
plugins.description: Security for web apps: OWASP-aligned code review (injection, XSS, CSRF, authz vs authn, mass assignment, uploads, secrets, dependency audit) mapped to PHP/Laravel and JS/Vue, PLUS design-phase threat-modeling (STRIDE, trust boundaries), a data-privacy (GDPR/CCPA) regulatory lens, and an api-auth lens (token model, OAuth2+PKCE, scopes). Includes /security:review and a security-engineer worker agent.

plugins.name: node-backend
plugins.description: Server-side Node.js best practices for Express 5, NestJS 11, and Fastify 5: middleware vs DI vs plugin-encapsulation architecture, async error propagation, validation at the boundary (zod, class-validator, JSON Schema), streaming and backpressure, graceful shutdown, config/env discipline, per-framework footguns.

plugins.name: vite
plugins.description: Vite best practices: VITE_-prefix env security, dep pre-bundling, code splitting and manualChunks, base for sub-path deploys, dev server.proxy, define stringify pitfalls, import.meta.glob, asset handling, build.target alignment, SSR, library mode, plugin order, HMR guards, version-aware against the locked vite version and vite.config. Includes /vite:review.

plugins.name: inertia
plugins.description: Inertia.js v1/v2/v3 best practices (Laravel + Vue/React/Svelte adapters): partial reloads, deferred and lazy props, useForm flow, shared data via middleware, prop hygiene, SSR, code splitting, v1/v2/v3 differences and adapter awareness. Includes /inertia:review.

plugins.name: api-design
plugins.description: REST API design: resource naming, status-code discipline, pagination/filtering/sorting conventions, versioning strategy, RFC 9457 error format, idempotency, Laravel API Resources, plus a graphql-grpc skill for non-REST surfaces (DataLoader, resolver authz, proto field-number safety, streaming). Includes /api-design:review and /api-design:scaffold (spec-first: OpenAPI → Laravel routes/FormRequests/Resources). Defers third-party API docs to api-docs-first.

plugins.name: dev-env
plugins.description: Dev environment initiator: scan composer/npm manifests, lockfiles, .env DSNs, and CI images, then generate a docker-compose.yml and Dockerfile matched to the actual stack — PHP version and extensions, Node, database engine, Redis, queues, mail. Includes /dev-env:init to generate and /dev-env:review to audit existing docker files. Pairs with stack-scan. Owns local development environments; defers CI/CD pipelines and production deploys to the devops plugin.

plugins.name: web-dev
plugins.description: Generalist web development pair: a web-developer worker (routing, REST/API integration, forms, state, SSR/CSR) and a frontend-reviewer that audits React/Vue/Inertia/Livewire/TS + react-native/vite against the matching per-framework skill. Stack-agnostic; defers stack idioms to the per-framework plugins.

plugins.name: system-design
plugins.description: System-level design: service boundaries on data ownership, scaling paths, cache placement, sync vs async integration and its failure modes, single points of failure, plus domain modeling (bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language) and an event-driven skill (delivery semantics, outbox, sagas, DLQ) — firing system-design, domain-modeling, and event-driven skills, a /system-design:review command, and a system-architect worker + system-design-reviewer pair. Complements code-architecture (code-level structure) without overlapping it.

plugins.name: devops
plugins.description: DevOps pipeline and infrastructure: CI/CD ordering, container/image hygiene, Kubernetes resource limits and probes, deploy strategy with rollback, and secrets handling — a firing devops-practices skill, a /devops:review command, and a devops-engineer worker + devops-reviewer pair. Owns infra-layer observability wiring (defers in-code instrumentation to observability); defers local docker-compose dev environments to dev-env.

plugins.name: database
plugins.description: Database implementation and safety for relational stores: a /database:review command, a database-engineer worker that applies schema, migration, indexing and pooling work, and a PreToolUse guard that asks for confirmation before a destructive statement (DROP/TRUNCATE/unqualified DELETE-UPDATE) lands. The design and statement rubric itself lives in the sql plugin's sql-best-practices skill; dialect audits in mysql/mariadb/postgresql.

plugins.name: performance
plugins.description: Performance tuning: measure-first profiling, N+1/index/payload/bundle/Core Web Vitals hotspots, cache correctness (stampede, TTL, eviction, staleness), and percentile load testing — a firing performance-tuning skill, a /performance:review command, and a worker agent that optimizes only what a measurement proves slow.

plugins.name: claude-authoring
plugins.description: Authoring guides for Claude Code artifacts — skills, agents, commands, hooks, plugins — plus a routine-detector that suggests scaffolding a project skill when work turns repetitive, a project-skill-suggester that proactively offers one when a task's cards share uncovered repository-specific knowledge, and /claude-authoring:new-skill|new-agent|new-command|new-hook|new-plugin scaffold commands.

plugins.name: code-review
plugins.description: Stack-agnostic code review: correctness bugs, code smells, convention drift on any diff or PR — severity-sorted one-line findings. Defers structure/YAGNI to code-architecture, security depth to security, stack idioms to the per-framework review plugins. Includes /code-review:review, a code-reviewer agent, and a code-smells skill. The fan-in for overlapping review surfaces: loads every installed matching stack skill in one pass.

plugins.name: approaches
plugins.description: Solution-approach deliberation before non-trivial implementation: 2-3 structurally different approaches with trade-offs and a kill-trigger, a strategy catalog mapped to the risk each beats, a four-persona blind opinion round for refactor-shaped tasks — plus the merged pre-code disciplines: build-vs-buy checks, S/M/L/XL estimation, rollout planning, and design-pattern selection. Includes /approaches:compare, /approaches:opinions, /approaches:build-vs-buy, /approaches:size, /approaches:rollout, /approaches:pattern.

plugins.name: hindsight
plugins.description: Cross-session self-improvement loop: mines session transcripts for recurring friction and proposes CLAUDE.md rules, skill/plugin ideas, and failed-approach warnings — applied only on approval.

plugins.name: brain
plugins.description: A committed, Obsidian-style codebase map for a project: brain/INDEX.md indexes areas, key files, and notable classes/entrypoints so a fresh Claude session starts oriented. A SessionStart hook injects the compact map (with a staleness hint when it lags HEAD); /brain reads it and /brain index builds/refreshes it. Builds the map only — it never annotates code, and nothing outside brain/ is ever modified.

plugins.name: resilience
plugins.description: Failure-mode design for integration points — timeouts, retries with backoff and idempotency, circuit breaking, graceful degradation, delivery semantics — plus the merged error-handling and concurrency disciplines: catches and cause chains, check-then-act races, retry idempotency. Includes /resilience:review, /resilience:error-review, /resilience:concurrency-review.

plugins.name: packages
plugins.description: Composer/npm dependency hygiene: semver constraint strategy, lockfile discipline, security-audit triage, dependency-licence checks against the project's distribution mode, and patch/minor/major upgrade lanes. Managing deps already in the project — whether to add one is build-vs-buy's job.

plugins.name: orchestration
plugins.description: Subagent orchestration discipline: delegation contracts (self-contained prompts, compressed evidence-backed returns, model/effort tiering, scout-then-fanout, writer isolation), verification panels (refuter voting, judge panels, loop-until-dry, completeness critic), plus the shared contract review commands route their fix lists through. Includes /orchestration:review.

plugins.name: a11y
plugins.description: Dedicated accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA audit for markup, contrast, keyboard navigation, focus management, forms, media, and ARIA — one line per violation with the concrete fix — plus an a11y-engineer worker that applies the fix list, preferring native semantics over ARIA patches and tagging each change with its WCAG criterion. Includes /a11y:audit.

plugins.name: observability
plugins.description: Application observability with judgment: structured JSON logs with correlation IDs, log levels that mean something, RED/USE metrics without cardinality bombs, trace-context propagation, symptom-based alerting, honest health checks — plus an observability-engineer worker that adds the instrumentation (deferring infra-layer wiring to devops). Includes /observability:review.

plugins.name: comment-discipline
plugins.description: Stops over-commenting by treating it as an information-routing problem: every fact goes to the artifact that cannot lie about it — a name, a type, a test, an extracted function — and comments are spent only on what has nowhere else to live: why-not-the-obvious-way, external constraints carrying a link or ticket, intentional-silence markers, and contract facts a signature cannot express. Kills restatement comments, section banners, commented-out code, bare TODOs, docblock tags that repeat the signature, and change-narration comments that describe the edit rather than the code. One hook, two lanes: PostToolUse warns on every category as code is written, and PreToolUse denies just the two strictest — a comment restating the next line, and commented-out code — once per file per session, so a false positive costs one turn and never wedges a run. A second warn-only hook extends the same routing rule to the terminal: it measures prose-per-tool-call against a calibrated threshold and says so once when a session narrates instead of reporting. Includes /comment-discipline:review.

plugins.name: candor
plugins.description: Candour as a mechanism, not a pep talk. A blocking Stop gate carries the two dishonesty shapes a script can prove: a file:line citation resolving to no file under cwd or to a line past the file's end, and a position retracted after challenge-shaped pushback with no tool call in between. Flattery openers, apologies, defensive phrasing and emotional intensifiers are counted by /candor:check and blocked by nothing, on purpose. Ships the straight-talk skill: six orderings, not sentiments. Completion claims stay with code-architecture.

plugins.name: lean
plugins.description: Prices every output as a debit and asks how much. Five surfaces, one bar each: code, tests, comments, files, and actions — a tool call, subagent spawn or verify pass whose result cannot change the next step is a paid no-op, and nothing else here prices that. Only four things buy more than the minimum: blast radius, an observed defect, a stated criterion, the user asking; the excess must name which, where it happens. Minimum means risk coverage, not count — never delete a test to hit a ratio.

plugins.name: frontend-suite
plugins.description: Meta-bundle: the frontend stack category in one install — UI/UX stacks, React, React Native, Vue 3, Next.js, Nuxt, Vite, Inertia, Livewire, the generalist web worker, accessibility auditing, and skill auto-routing (skill-router). The creative-build studio — craft-layer, design-preview, shadcn-studio, registry-source, threejs — moved to craft-suite, so ordinary frontend app work does not pay the studio's always-on context. Uninstall cleanly with /frontend-suite:uninstall — removes the bundle and prunes its auto-installed plugins.

plugins.name: craft-suite
plugins.description: Meta-bundle: the creative-build studio in one install — concept-first creative direction with a tiered motion catalog (craft-layer), visual decisions rendered with the project's own components (design-preview), a shadcn staging sandbox (shadcn-studio), live component-registry MCP sourcing (registry-source), and WebGL/Three.js effects (threejs), plus the two companions the studio requires: ui-ux and a11y. Split out of frontend-suite so ordinary frontend app work does not pay the studio's always-on context. Uninstall cleanly with /craft-suite:uninstall — removes the bundle and prunes its auto-installed plugins.

plugins.name: php-suite
plugins.description: Meta-bundle: the PHP category in one install — PHP and Laravel best practices, Livewire, Inertia, Vite (Laravel's default asset bundler), and the generalist web worker. Uninstall cleanly with /php-suite:uninstall — removes the bundle and prunes its auto-installed plugins.

plugins.name: db-suite
plugins.description: Meta-bundle: the database category in one install — engine-agnostic SQL discipline, MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL best practices, and the database worker agent. Uninstall cleanly with /db-suite:uninstall — removes the bundle and prunes its auto-installed plugins.

plugins.name: product-suite
plugins.description: Meta-bundle: the product-domain disciplines in one install — payments and billing (idempotent webhooks, money handling, ledgers), internationalization (ICU MessageFormat, Intl, RTL), and LLM application engineering (evals, RAG, prompt-injection defense). Uninstall cleanly with /product-suite:uninstall — removes the bundle and prunes its auto-installed plugins.

plugins.name: quality-suite
plugins.description: Meta-bundle: the code-quality plugins that carry an enforcement mechanism — review and code smells with the single-pass fan-in, architecture's evidence-at-claim Stop gate, candor's citation-and-reversal Stop gate, comment discipline (warn-on-write plus a narrow pre-write deny), destructive-command blocking, secret-leak prevention, a token-cost warn hook (lean), and file-aware skill auto-routing. The advisory nine — security, a11y, debugging, performance, resilience, packages, observability, approaches, testing — live in quality-principles-suite; the membership rule is prose, not script-checked. Uninstall cleanly with /quality-suite:uninstall — removes the bundle and prunes its auto-installed plugins.

plugins.name: quality-principles-suite
plugins.description: Meta-bundle: the code-quality disciplines that advise rather than enforce — approach deliberation and design patterns, OWASP security review and threat modeling, WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, systematic debugging, measure-first performance, resilience with the merged error-handling and concurrency disciplines, dependency hygiene, observability, and test design and coverage review (testing — moved here in 0.2.0; it ships no enforcement hook; the membership rule itself is prose, not script-checked). Split out of quality-suite so a project can take the enforcing half without the advisory half's always-on context. Uninstall cleanly with /quality-principles-suite:uninstall — removes the bundle and prunes its auto-installed plugins.

plugins.name: process-suite
plugins.description: Meta-bundle: the engineering-process category in one install — git workflow, approach deliberation (with the build-vs-buy, estimation, rollout, and pattern-selection disciplines folded into approaches), hindsight mining, docs upkeep, subagent orchestration, task execution, stack scanning, plugin scouting, a token-cost warn hook (lean), and file-aware skill auto-routing (skill-router). Uninstall cleanly with /process-suite:uninstall — removes the bundle and prunes its auto-installed plugins.

plugins.name: everything
plugins.description: Meta-bundle: installs every plugin in this marketplace as a dependency — all stacks, all workflows, all agents. One install, full suite. Uninstall cleanly with /everything:uninstall — removes the bundle and prunes its auto-installed plugins.

plugins.name: taskmaster-suite
plugins.description: Meta-bundle (31 plugins): the full clarification-to-execution workflow plus its wired companions — taskmaster, task-runner, stack-scan, code-architecture, the review and process plugins (code-review, git-workflow, orchestration, approaches, and the rest), and the ui-ux agents the pipeline's visual cards route to. Uninstall cleanly with /taskmaster-suite:uninstall — removes the bundle and prunes its auto-installed plugins.

plugins.name: skill-router
plugins.description: File-aware skill auto-routing: a PostToolUse hook injects one additionalContext directive to load the relevant best-practice skill(s) when you edit a matching file (PHP/Laravel/Blade, React/Vue/Inertia/Livewire via .tsx/.jsx/.vue, plain .ts/.js/.py/.go/.rb/.rs, SQL and migrations with engine-aware MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL rows, components, tests, Dockerfiles, OpenAPI), a SessionStart hook primes a repo-tailored skill index, and low-confidence content signals flush as one digest on your next prompt (SessionEnd keeps the ledger). Every relevant skill co-fires per edit; fail-open, once per skill per session.

plugins.name: command-guard
plugins.description: Destructive-command prevention: a PreToolUse hook that classifies every Bash (and MCP shell/SQL) command before it runs — denying irreversible data loss (migrate:fresh, db:wipe, DROP DATABASE, rm -rf /, git clean -fdx, docker compose down -v, terraform destroy, cloud deletes) and prompting on scoped-but-destructive ones (git reset --hard, rm -rf ./dir, kubectl delete pod). Reads through quotes, wrappers and heredocs; skips read-only commands; fail-open. Ships /command-guard:check and a user-owned allow-file the agent cannot edit.

plugins.name: secret-scanning
plugins.description: Secret-leak prevention: a PreToolUse hook that blocks a Write/Edit introducing a high-confidence secret (cloud keys, private-key blocks, provider tokens, assigned secret literals) before it reaches disk, plus a /secret-scanning:scan command to sweep a path or diff on demand. Fail-open, high-confidence-only, with a fixture escape.

plugins.name: payments
plugins.description: Payments and billing discipline (Stripe/Paddle/Braintree): PCI scope minimization via tokenization, integer-minor-unit money, signature-verified idempotent webhooks, subscription state machines and activation races, dunning and proration, and an append-only ledger with reconciliation — a firing payments skill and a /payments:review command. The failure class is double-charges and revenue leaks.

plugins.name: i18n
plugins.description: Internationalization and localization: semantic translation keys and catalog hygiene, ICU MessageFormat pluralization and gender, locale-aware dates/numbers/currency via Intl, RTL layout with logical properties, fallback chains, and tooling-driven extraction — a firing i18n skill and a /i18n:review command. For products shipping outside one language; skips a genuinely single-locale app.

plugins.name: llm-app
plugins.description: LLM application engineering: eval harnesses and regression gates (evaluate, don't eyeball), RAG pipelines (chunking, embeddings, retrieval quality + re-ranking, grounding and citation), prompt versioning, prompt-injection defense, token-cost control, and context management — a firing llm-app skill and a /llm-app:review command. Defers provider API specifics to Claude Code's built-in claude-api skill (harness-provided, not part of this marketplace).

plugins.name: ultra-deep-research
plugins.description: Deep-research harness that fans out parallel web searches, tiers sources by provenance, extracts date-stamped claims, and adversarially refutes them before synthesizing a cited report with a contradiction ledger and per-section confidence. Trigger 'ultra-deep-research' escalates to a Workflow-driven loop-until-dry fan-out with multi-vote refutation panels; standard depth runs a portable parallel-Agent fan-out. Ships /ultra-deep-research:research plus researcher and verifier subagents. Writes the report inline and to research/<topic>-<date>.md.

plugins.name: threejs
plugins.description: Three.js best practices: WebGPURenderer-first with automatic WebGL2 fallback (WebGPU is Baseline since Jan 2026), TSL shaders, react-three-fiber/drei integration, asset pipelines (glTF/Draco/KTX2), disposal and leak discipline, render-loop and draw-call performance, version-aware against the locked three revision. Includes /threejs:review.

plugins.name: fresh-take
plugins.description: Independent stronger-model second opinion at key moments — stuck debugging or an imminent irreversible action. /fresh-take:consult composes a facts-only brief (no leaning) and dispatches a blind stronger-model consultant with read-only repo access; it returns a Take, Risks, and one Alternative. A UserPromptSubmit reminder hook nudges the command on key-moment phrases. Advice only — it never blocks, gates, or edits anything.

plugins.name: terse
plugins.description: Chat-message brevity as a shape contract, not a word filter: prose-line budgets per turn kind, a fixed work-done skeleton (verdict → artifacts → max 5 findings → blocker → next), and a named cut list. Levels lite/full/ultra plus wenyan (classical-Chinese novelty) variants, hook-reinforced each turn. Out of scope: code, files written, subagent prompts, and how much work a turn does. Ships /terse:commit, /terse:compress, /terse:check, three compressed-return agents, and an opt-in MCP catalog shrinker.
